[kathā + ujja], discussion; dispute; Sn 825 (vadenti te aññasitā ~aṃ; Nidd I 163,.21 : ~aṃ vuccati kalaho bhaṇḍanaṃ …); 828 (virame ~aṃ); —       °-pacchindana,   n., putting an end to talk; Sp 1406,.4 (~’-atthaṃ); —       °-pavatti,   f., the course of conversation, progress of a discussion; Ja I 119,.19; Sp 587,.27; Pj II 538,.33 (hotu no bho kāci ~ī ti); —       °-pābhata,   n., a story to tell; a story worth telling; D III 118,.15 (atthi kho idaṃ … ~aṃ bhagavantaṃ dassanāya; Sv 908,.22 : ~an ti kathāya mūlaṃ); Ja I 252,.4; Pj II 356,.10; —       °-phāsuka,   mfn., easy to talk to; with whom one can converse comfortably; Ja VI 23,23´ (~ena amaccasaṅghena parivutaṃ); Sp 216,.28 (yassa vissāsikā ~ā bhikkhū); Spk I 35,.4 (nisajjaphāsukaṃ ~aṃ dutiyakaṃ alabhantī); —       °-vatthu1,   n., a subject for a discourse or a story; a subject of conversation; M I 372,.35; II 107,.21 (idaṃ ~uṃ anupubbena rājantepuraṃ pāvisi); A I 197,.11; Mp I 134,.6 (dasa ~ūni); —       °-vatthu2,   n., ~-ppakaraṇa, n., the name of the fifth of the books making up the Abhidhammapiṭaka; the book of debates; Kv 628,.4 (~-ppakaraṇe pañcatiṃsabhāṇavāraṃ niṭṭhitaṃ); Mil 12,28 (āyasmā ca Nāgaseno … suttasahassaṃ samodhānetvā vibhattaṃ ~-ppakkaraṇaṃ … paguṇaṃ katvā); Vism 692,.28 (uttaraṃ abhidhamme ~usmiṃ vuttam eva); Sp 18,.18 (… ~u yamakaṃ paṭṭhānan ti idaṃ abhidhammapiṭakaṃ nāma); 61,.13 (Moggaliputta-tissatthero parappavādaṃ maddamāno ~-ppakaraṇaṃ abhāsi); Ud-a 94,.9 (vitthāro … ~-pakaraṇassa ṭīkāya gahetabbo, Be, Se so; Ce, Ee kathāvatthū-); As 3,.25 (vitaṇḍavādī pan’ āha ~u kasmā gahitaṃ, nanu sammāsambuddhassa parinibbānato aṭṭhārasa-vassādhikāni dve vassasatāni atikkamitvā Moggaliputtatissattheren’ etaṃ ṭhapitaṃ, Be, Se so; Ce, Ee ~uṃ); 4,.29 (Moggaliputtatissatthero nāma bhikkhu … suttasahassaṃ samodhānetvā dīghanikāyappamāṇaṃ ~-ppakaraṇaṃ bhājessatī ti); Ap-a 274,.19 foll. (~-visuddhiyā ti ~-ppakaraṇe visuddhiyā cheko … dasasu ~ūsu vā cheko; ad Ap 37,.1); — ~-ppakaraṇavaṇṇanā, f., the commentary on the Kathāvatthu; Kv-a 202,.11 (~-ppakaraṇavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā, Ce, Ee so; Be ~-atthakathā; Se ~-ppakaraṇatthakathā); —       °-samuṭṭhāna,   n., the arising of a discussion; Pj II 260,.17; Mhv 5:138; —       °-samuṭṭhāpana,   n., starting a conversation; instigating a discussion or talk; Ja III 278,.4 (~’-atthaṃ); Ud-a 120,.8 (bhagavā ~’-atthaṃ pucchanto); —       °-sallāpa,   m., conversation; dialogue; Vin I 77,.31 (assosi … mātāpitunnaṃ imaṃ ~aṃ); D I 89,.27 (evarūpehi kulaputtehi saddhiṃ ~o; Sv 276,.17 : ~o ti kathā ca sallāpo ca, kathanapaṭikathanan ti attho); M I 178,.2; Ja II 283,.19; Mil 31,.24 (kimhi hoti ~o ti); —       °-sīsa,   n., the head word of a statement or exposition; Sadd 690,.18 (vantussā ti hi ~-mattaṃ vuttaṃ); —      dukkathā,   f., a wrong discourse, harmful talk; A III 181,.4 (assaddhassa … saddhākathā ~ā); —      sukathā,   f., a good discourse, well-directed talk; A III 182,.12.

1dhamma
m. (and n.) [S., BHS dharma], dhamma denotes (an interpretation of) the essential nature and reality of existence and experience, the way things are: it is descriptive and prescriptive; it denotes also an essential attribute of men or animals; a quality or characteristic; Abh 784 (~o sabhāve pariyattipaññāñāyesu saccappakatīsu puññe ñeyye guṇācārasamādhisū pi nissattatāpattisu kāraṇādo); see also Sv 99,.3 foll., Ps I 17,.16 foll., It-a I 37,.20 foll., Paṭis-a 18,.1 foll., Bv-a 13,.4 foll., As 38,.23 foll. and Sadd 560,.25 foll.; — for Buddhists dhamma is used to denote an interlocking and interdependent assembly of concepts: the true nature of the world of experience, how that world works, and the way to transcend it, as understood by the Buddha; the progressive stages of understanding and nibbāna ; the behaviour, the practice, required to achieve understanding of the way the world of experience works, ie the way to reach arhatship, nibbāna ; the understanding and practice taught by the Buddha, the substance of his teaching, the texts of the Canon, especially the Suttapiṭaka ; all constituents of the world of experience, physical and mental, external and internal, progressively more and more minutely analysed; all constituents of prescribed practice, appropriate and beneficial actions; prescriptions for the members of the saṅgha ; — for people generally dhamma is an interpretation of the essential nature of existence and experience; the way one should act, depending on who one is, to maintain the way things are and should be; duty; right; justice; normative and beneficial actions; — 1. (i) how the world of experience works, the processes by which it works and is explained (especially as formulated in cattāri ariyasaccāni and paṭiccasamuppāda ), and the possibility and way of transcending it, as understood by the Buddha and taught by him (so that knowledge and understanding of it might bring enlightenment, arhatship, to others); Vin I 2,3* (yadā have pātubhavanti ~ā ātāpino jhāyato brāhmaṇassa ath’ assa kaṅkhā vapayanti sabbā yato pajānāti sahetudhammaṃ; Sp 954,.19 foll. : pātubhavantī ti uppajjanti ~ā ti anulomapaccayākārapaṭivedhasādhakā bodhipakkhiyadhammā, atha vā pātubhavantī ti pakāsenti abhisamayavasena vyattā pākaṭā honti, ~ā ti caturāriyasaccadhammā); 11,.2 (idaṃ dukkhaṃ ariyasaccan ti me bhikkhave pubbe ananussutesu ~esu cakkhuṃ udapādi); 12,.24 (ehi bhikkhū ti bhagavā avoca svākkhāto ~o cara brahmacariyaṃ sammā dukkhassa antakiriyāyā ti); 15,.31 (idaṃ kho Yasa anupaddutaṃ idaṃ anupassaṭṭhaṃ ehi Yasa nisīda ~aṃ te desessāmī ti); 40,.19 foll.
